That is the sharpest constraint in the registry, and it decides seat assignment rather than merely annotating it: a seat on this harness should produce judgement for a human or another model to read, not a record to be parsed, which is exactly why the reviewer seat fits it and a scribe seat does not. **One correction to a shipped row**: `--max-turns` is *not present* in the Claude Code binary measured here, though it appears in documentation — so §7.4b no longer says "bind the harness's turn and spend ceilings" but "bind whichever actually exist, and check the registry rather than assuming symmetry". A deployment budgeting by turn count would have been budgeting with a flag that is not there. **One capability found rather than corrected**: `--bg`/`--background` plus a `claude agents` management surface is an in-product background-agent supervisor, which is why §13 already lists the bespoke supervisor as a prunable unit — a deployment should evaluate the built-in before building one. **And a new cross-harness mechanism, measured rather than read**: a long-lived process holds the PATH snapshot it inherited at start, so a harness installed *or self-updated into a new directory* afterwards is invisible to it even though the user PATH carries the entry. Three entries were present in the registry PATH and absent from the live process on this host, one of them a CLI that had just self-updated — which had made it look uninstalled. A desk launcher MUST therefore resolve harness binaries by absolute path recorded per host, because the failure mode presents as a configuration error rather than a stale environment. Local-endpoint fitness was measured on the same pass and the result is FIT: a locally-served model emitted correct tool calls with correct arguments, chose the right tool of two, honoured a JSON schema, and declined to call a tool when none was needed — so the `local` lane is real rather than aspirational for T4 observation seats. verify-nway 23-axis PASS.
- **v2.6.2** (2026-07-25) — **The credential rule says what it can actually say (Corporate v0.1.2)** — v2.6.1's §9.1 over-read its own evidence. The vendor language it cited prohibits three specific things — sharing credentials, offering a consumer sign-in to third parties, and routing other parties' requests through a personal entitlement — and the spec turned that into a near-prohibition on resident seats backed by a subscription, which the same vendors contradict by shipping, documenting and maintaining non-interactive modes in their own first-party CLIs. A subscriber driving their own subscription through the flag the vendor published is *using the vendor's application*. So §9.1 is rewritten around the distinction it should have drawn from the start: **what a vendor prohibits is a fact for the spec; how intensely an operator drives their own subscription is that operator's judgment.** The prohibition list stays and stays absolute — credential extraction and relay remain excluded from the module's architecture at the spec level, because that is the one place the prohibitions actually bite a design, and a seat that serves requests which are not the operator's own is moved to the automation lane by the list rather than by preference. What changes is that the lanes are now a **routing distinction rather than a permission boundary**: an interactive-lane resident seat is legitimate, `lane` is required as a *declaration* with a one-line rationale rather than as a verdict the spec hands down, and the knob that actually governs intensity — `fanoutCeiling` — remains mandatory precisely because the lane choice is not. A third lane is named: **`local`**, an endpoint on the operator's own machine, which raises no entitlement question at all and removes the §7.4b per-wake billing pressure entirely — making it the natural home for high-duty-cycle, low-judgment seats (resident and scheduled T4 observation, whose job is deciding whether to wake something more expensive). Its trade is capability rather than permission, so tool-calling fitness is confirmed per serving stack and per model rather than per family. One prohibition is deliberately left asymmetric: a free tier that trains on submitted content is still never assigned a resident or production seat, because being wrong there publishes the project rather than exceeding a quota. verify-nway 23-axis PASS.
- **v2.6.1** (2026-07-25) — **The harness registry gets its rows (Corporate v0.1.1)** — v2.6.0 shipped Corporate with every harness in `caveats`, because §9's first rule is that a row requires a source and no invocation string had been confirmed verbatim. This cut discharges that: **four confirmed harnesses** (Claude Code, Codex CLI, Antigravity CLI, Gemini CLI) with non-interactive flags, session-continuation syntax, path grants, instruction-discovery order, per-invocation model/effort/budget binding, and the `gotchas` that break a naive desk implementation — among them that resuming a session does **not** restore `--add-dir`, `--mcp-config`, `--settings` or `--plugin-dir`, so a resident seat's launcher must keep its whole flag set rather than just a session id; and that two ways of granting a directory are **not equivalent** (one also loads that directory's skills, agents and plugin settings, the other grants file access only). Eight gaps stay in `caveats` instead of being guessed at. Five `crossHarnessFacts` record what holds everywhere: instruction discovery runs root→cwd on every harness surveyed with no reversal switch — which is why §2.2 specifies **precedence** rather than load order; instruction budgets are small enough (a 200-line/25 KB memory index, a 32 KiB instruction cap) that a long charter silently truncates the thing it was meant to override; and one vendor already protects an agent's own configuration directories as read-only inside otherwise-writable roots, which is the precedent behind the no-self-configuration invariant. One entry is a warning rather than a row: Gemini CLI stopped serving consumer-plan requests as of 2026-06-18, so a seat on a consumer Google subscription belongs on Antigravity CLI. verify-nway 23-axis PASS.
- **v2.6.0** (2026-07-25) — **Corporate — the third orchestration axis: who exists (new 7th module v0.1.0 + Constellation v2.4.90)** — EG had two orchestration layers and no way to say that a *job* exists. Superscalar's unit is a lane: anonymous, alive for one fan-out, structurally unable to accumulate anything. Constellation's unit is a process: it has an identity, but a process is not a job description — §13.9.3 separates wire role from duty and then stops, leaving "what is this agent *for*, across time" to prose in a charter. **Corporate** names the missing noun: the **durable role**, a seat that outlives any session or process and therefore gains four properties a lane cannot have — it accumulates practice, is addressable across time, can own units in a coordination registry, and gives a decision an addressee. Per this repo's own semver rubric (`Ultrasafe.md §10.3`: module addition = Tier 2 = MINOR) this is the cut that opens the **2.6 line**, filling the `2.6.x` slot `Greatpractice.md` had already reserved. **What ships is the durable half, deliberately.** The two-space desk contract — a **gitignored private desk** that is the cwd the role's harness actually runs in (charter, its own memory, session state) plus a **tracked public locker** that is the read surface for the organization and the user, the default sharing mechanism being *write a document and pass the path* rather than passing content by message. Multi-host organizations, where a desk deliberately **does not span hosts** (moving a seat is an eviction plus a re-creation, not a path edit; cross-host coordination goes through the board or the wire, never a remote mount; the locker is the cross-host exchange). Four **residency classes** defaulting to the cheapest, with an organization circuit breaker that **demotes rather than stops** — reusing the shape *and the field name* of Superscalar §5.2's auto-demotion, because divergent names for identical mechanics are a documentation defect. A **three-layer toggle chain** (role > group > organization) whose discipline is *many layers, exactly one resolver*: layering is not mirroring, and nothing but `resolve.cjs` reads a layer. That resolver carries the **identity invariant** — with no roster present, resolution returns the organization layer verbatim, so a project that never adopts Corporate behaves bit-identically to one where the module does not exist. §5.4 makes it a **test obligation rather than a claim**, and `--selftest` discharges it: fixtures in a temp directory (never the caller's project), identity stated as two non-circular properties against the raw marker files — nothing dropped or altered, nothing invented — plus precedence, per-key object merge, and the rule that a `defaults` block never displaces a legacy marker. And **eviction specified at the same level as creation** (§7.4), shipped in the first cut as a *skill* rather than a footnote: creation fires on a frequent signal (work arrives that no seat fits) while dissolution fires on a backward-looking one (nothing happened here for a while), and an unautomated backward-looking check does not run — so a **dynamic** organization MUST have a scheduled sweep, human disposal on the gate surface, a declared seat ceiling, and a per-seat record of the justifying signal (§7.5). The sweep raises candidates; a human disposes. **Constellation v2.4.90 (§13.33)** carries the wire side: two events joining the existing declaration class (`CommandManifest`/`CapabilityManifest`/`OpsState`) with mechanics unchanged — `CorporateChart` (structure, main-only) and `RoleState` (per-seat liveness) — so an organization whose roster is local and gitignored reaches a board that hosts none of it, **including a peer's board**. Render invariants make the honest failure visible: **absence renders as unknown, never as idle** (the §13.31 render-fallback lesson in a new place — a surface looks healthiest exactly when the data is missing), only declared fields render, node tier/model/effort show *resolved* values never one layer of the chain, and `deskRef` is an opaque label rather than a filesystem path. `taskRef` points at a board entry id so the chart and the work registry agree **by reference rather than by restatement**. **The perishable half is a data file, not spec prose** (§9): exact invocation flags, session-continuation syntax, sandbox-grant keys and instruction-file names live in `harness-registry.json` under Superscalar §5.1.3's three rules (a row requires a source URL; bind per invocation never by global pin; the file states its own expiry) — so the spec does not rot on harness release cadence, and this cut ships every harness in `caveats` rather than inventing a flag, because the honest failure for an unresolved harness is a **refusal to launch**. The module also states its own non-adoption (§15): below three thresholds a Superscalar fan-out plus a board is cheaper, and a single-developer project with one recurring duty wants a scribe rather than an organization. Also here: the practice-role derivation runs **both ways** (§8) — a recorded practice is evidence a seat is warranted, so bootstrap proposes roles from the project's measured work history rather than from imagination, and the same signal inverted is an eviction trigger. **An 8-axis research pass with per-axis adversarial verification (17 agents) reshaped the spec before it shipped, and the corrections are the most load-bearing parts of it.** (1) **Role text is a routing signal and an attachment point, never a capability claim** (§3.4) — large-scale trace analysis puts *role-specification violation* at the **bottom** of fourteen failure classes (~1.5%) while missing verification (~17%), step repetition (~16%), reasoning-action mismatch (~13%) and **unrecognised termination conditions** (~12%) dominate, and measured gains came from rewiring the workflow (+9%) and adding task-level verification (+16%) rather than from adding roles; persona-based capability improvement is a negative result twice over. So the spec forbids capability claims, makes a **verification seat default (its absence is a lint warning)**, and promotes **termination conditions and a stall counter to first-class fields**. The role table is deliberately short, and a longer roster is not a better one. (2) **What crosses an edge is a trace, not a message** (§6.6) — the strongest published objection to agent organizations is about context, not roles, and vendor guidance singles out dependency-heavy coding as the poorest fit. Absorbed rather than answered: `traceMode` is required **with no default**, `wiring` is per-edge (`directed`|`discretionary`) so the org chart and the passing rules stay separable, dependency density is a required decomposition input, and spans where parallel participants cannot see each other's implicit decisions must be enumerated with parallelism forbidden inside them. Instruction-level width limits are measurably useless, so fan-out caps belong to a runtime guard. (3) **Write ownership is partitioned by file** (§6.7) — `owns[]` required, union disjoint, CAS for shared state, per-item queue validation with bad-item quarantine. (4) **Two credential lanes** (§9.1) — subscription sign-in is licensed for ordinary individual use of the vendor's own applications and metered keys are the documented programmatic surface, so interactive and automation lanes are declared per seat, **credential extraction/relay is excluded at the spec level**, `fanoutCeiling` is declared with a rationale, and a free tier that trains on submitted content is never assigned a resident seat. (5) **Supply chain** (§9.2) — a real ~40-minute credential-stealer release in a widely-used proxy, and service wrappers variously years-unmaintained, make the proxy host a declared blast radius, wrappers a replaceable adapter boundary rather than a recommended default, shared stores read-only by default, and **self-modification of a seat's own configuration a MUST-NOT**. (6) **Cost has a shape** (§7.4b) — same-output overhead ~1.15–2.3× versus ~4×/~7×/~15× for agent/team/exploration, reported separately because collapsing them locks the gate against the wrong thing; and since an active seat bills until terminated, **terminate and evict are different verbs** (§7.4c). (7) **Gates are precise, not voluminous** (§12.1) — irreversible calls are well under 1% of tool use while intervention on ~4% carries the largest quality gain, and **an approval relayed by a participant is not an approval**. (8) An honest correction: the natural phrasing "load the charter before the project file" is **not achievable** — discovery is fixed root→cwd on every harness surveyed — so §2.2 now specifies **precedence** (run the harness in the desk so the charter merges last and nearest-wins) and forbids claiming a reversed order. And (9) §15.1 states **four conditions under which the correct output is no organization at all**, because the rubric that can reject an organization is at least as much of this module as the path that builds one. verify-nway grows to **23 axes** (new Corporate module+plugin axis; seed registry 7 modules; docs-badge and docs-meta extended) and caught its own cut mid-flight — the Constellation bump surfaced two stale docs surfaces before commit. Seed marker v2.5.1 → v2.6.0 across all six tiers.
- **v2.5.208** (2026-07-25) — **Refusal is now spoken, authority is now visible, History states its own scope (Constellation v2.4.89)** — the adopter's follow-up appendix reported the failure that had bitten *them*: a keyless remote connection to a `requireKey` board looked like a success — SERVER_HELLO arrived, AgentList arrived, the send raised nothing, the socket closed normally — while the board recorded only their AgentHello and never their report. They believed they had filed it. Root cause measured here: the requireKey check **closed the socket with no reason**, so frames pipelined in the same burst after HELLO died in transport rather than being refused by policy; and because the close carried no code, it was indistinguishable from a normal one. (Their inferred cause — `requireKey=false` accepting a connection at null authority — was not the mechanism; the board had requireKey ON. The symptom class they named was real, the attribution was one layer off.) Three fixes, all of them their proposals: **(1) refusal speaks** — both HELLO-time rejections (IP-not-allowlisted, key-required) now emit `ConnectionRejected{reason, surface, hint}`, flush it, then close with **code 4403**, and the hint names the setting plus warns that follow-ups will not be relayed; `close()` in the WS core gained RFC6455 code/reason support to make that possible. **(2) authority is visible** — a successful HELLO now returns `ConnectionInfo{agentId, role, surface, mayManageKeys, mayRelayTargeted, keyed, historyScope}`, so a client never has to infer its own permissions, which is the condition that let an invalid send read as a successful one. **(3) History declares its abridgement** — the payload gains `scope{policy, activeEvents, coldChannels, archivedChannels, note}`, because the previous silent scoping led the adopter to conclude the board's History simply did not carry A2A. - **v2.5.67** (2026-06-07) — **Constellation v2.4.7 single-workspace multi-agent session-aware routing (register-all + fail-safe) + dashboard issuance bug fix** — when multiple Claude Code sessions (main + local worker, etc.) are open in the same workspace, they share-execute the same Stop hook (`pre-send-probe --rearm`) → contention on the same A2A cursor (a worker turn-end advances main's surfacing cursor first → main never sees the inbound; surface theft). Avoids splitting into separate workspaces (duplicate extension loading per IDE window + harness/doc context severance cost) by branching on the **per-session env `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID`** (injected into the hook process by Claude Code — `src=env` empirically confirmed, stdin payload `.session_id` fallback). **register-all model**: every session (main included) declares its own inboxes in the `<cwd>/.agent-sessions.json` registry; each hook run processes only SELF-owned inboxes — (a) unregistered/unidentifiable session → SKIP-ALL (fail-safe: no cursor advance, never intrudes on another session's surface — main protection guaranteed by mechanism, not discipline), (b) inbox owned by another session → skip, (c) ownerless inbox → skip (register-all requires explicit ownership), (d) self-owned → normal processing. When the registry is inactive (absent/empty workers), legacy default (single-session workspace, identical to before) — back-compat. **New/changed files**: `runtime/stop-hook/register-session.cjs` (NEW — registers/validates/releases session `{role, ownInboxes}`, keyed by `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID`) + `runtime/stop-hook/pre-send-probe.cjs` (register-all routing block — 6/6 case simulation PASS) + `runtime/scripts/join-local.cjs` v2.4.7 (local worker `OUTBOX` drain = the worker session appends to the outbox file → join-local sends via a 1.5s drain, new worker emit path + full inbound logging so Delegate value bodies are read) + `runtime/server.cjs` (startup warning when WS_PRIMARY_AGENT is unset — when unset, the main session is demoted to local; mechanizes `feedback_self_board_restart_env`). **Two-tier wakeup for low-latency A2A inbox reception**: tier 1 = ≤5s polling file Monitor (immediate wakeup on event), tier 2 = long ScheduleWakeup fallback heartbeat (1200-1800s) — relying on ScheduleWakeup cadence (minute-scale) alone delays reception by that much (confirmed by the 2026-06-07 case where board-observer waited for a Delegate until the /loop cadence). **Dashboard issuance bug fix (Cut A bundle)**: blocked the `.ws-collab-*` cursor:move leak (`.ws-pop-head`'s cursor:move was inherited down the issuance panel's child chain — leak path confirmed via Playwright) + (private self-board) 5-handler drift fix for KEY-MGMT responses (root cause of key issuance stalling at "발급 중…" — the outer dashboard was missing the v2.4.0 canonical KeyIssued/KeyError/KeyListResult/KeyRevoked·Labeled·RevokePending handlers, confirmed via Playwright WS frame capture). **Live verification**: round-trip with the local worker (board-observer) — Delegate→WorkerAck/WorkerReport, **direct proof of main-cursor non-collision** (multiple worker turn-ends SKIP the collab-self inbox → main cursor held at 287; the worker's 3 replies remained unsurfaced and main's next hook surfaced them normally) + main auto-reception (≤3s file Monitor, no nudge). **Files modified**: Constellation.md(frontmatter v2.4.6 → v2.4.7 + codicil); plugins/constellation/.claude-plugin/plugin.json(v0.3.6 → v0.3.7); pre-send-probe.cjs + register-session.cjs(NEW) + scripts/join-local.cjs + server.cjs + dashboard/style.css; README(badge + Current/현재 EN+KO); docs/index.html(hero badge v2.5.66 → v2.5.67 + module-tag v2.4.6 → v2.4.7); docs/shared/data.js(v2.5.66 → v2.5.67 + shipCount 82 → 83); .claude-plugin/marketplace.json(metadata 0.3.12 → 0.3.13 + constellation v0.3.6 → v0.3.7); - **v2.5.44** (2026-06-04) — **`constellation/reference/runtime/stop-hook/pre-send-probe.cjs` self-emission echo filter — drop lines where `o.ev === "sent"` during meaningful classification. The bridge logs both outbound (`ev:"sent"`) and inbound (`ev:"inbound"`) to the same inbox.log file, so without this gate the §13.16.9 name-only allowlist (Report / Delegate / WorkerReport / Request / PRRequest / etc.) classified every outbox push as meaningful inbound on the next probe — a self-emission echo class that polluted the watch-state cycle.** Watch-state hygiene patch cut. Diagnosis: v2.4.16 (3565b32) removed a `grep '"ev":"in...'` 1st-stage gate because some adopter bridges write inbound without the `ev` marker; the removal correctly unblocked bridge-alive direct inbound, but it implicitly admitted self-emission `ev:"sent"` lines into the classification pipeline. The downstream §13.16.9 allowlist filters by message name only, so every outbound A2A-intent push (Report, Delegate, PRRequest, etc.) re-appeared as meaningful inbound on the next Stop hook fire — the agent's `feedback_pre_send_inbound_check.md` discipline then forced a "read meaningful body + classify" round-trip that costs context without supplying any new information, since the body was the agent's own just-sent payload. Real observed incident: after EG outbox push 348 (`m-eg-cycle1-ack-1780528600` Report to main), the next Stop hook surface listed line 23271 as meaningful — the very same Report content the agent had just composed. **Fix**: `if (o?.ev === 'sent') continue;` injected immediately after the `JSON.parse` step in `probe()` (lines 90-91 area). Per-line `ev:"sent"` SKIP, NOT an `ev:"inbound"` REQUIRE — adopters whose bridges write inbound without the `ev` marker continue to have their inbound surfaced normally (the v2.4.16 regression risk is preserved). Inline comment block documents the design choice + cross-references v2.4.16 + v2.5.20 doubly-wrapped envelope handling (orthogonal — `value.name` fallback still applies after the self-emission skip). **No protocol wire change** — this is a Stop hook reference-impl classification fix, not a §13.x specification change. - **v2.5.43** (2026-06-04) — **`constellation/reference/runtime/local-bridge.cjs` outboxCursor init aligned with `local-bridge.eux` `@state.outboxCursor` spec (init = EOF, pre-existing lines skipped on respawn). Closes a spec-vs-impl mismatch where the implementation initialized `outboxCursor = 0` at module init, causing the entire accumulated outbox.jsonl to be re-shipped on every bridge restart — §13.13.2 server-side dedup masked the application-level impact (every duplicate carried the same `msgId` and was rejected with `AckProcessed{dedupHit:true}`), but bandwidth + log noise was significant: a 19h disconnection window followed by respawn replayed 331 `ev:'sent'` entries in a single drain cycle in a real observed incident.** Bridge runtime patch cut. The `local-bridge.eux` `@state.outboxCursor` declaration documents the intended behavior as `byte offset already shipped from outbox (init = EOF so pre-existing lines are skipped)`, and `derive.connected_gate` reiterates `cursor inits at EOF`. The reference C implementation in `local-bridge.cjs` however set `let outboxCursor = 0;` at module init, then byte-offset-tailed from there — diverging from the spec by treating all pre-existing outbox content as un-shipped on every spawn. Adopters using the reference impl experienced the same backlog-replay behavior on every bridge restart; `feedback_a2a_relay_reliability.md`'s at-most-once relay note further compounds the concern (transport-tier `Ack delivered` does not guarantee recipient inbox has the body, but here the wire was carrying re-sends of already-acknowledged content). **Fix**: replaces `let outboxCursor = 0;` with `function initOutboxCursor() { try { return fs.statSync(OUTBOX).size; } catch { return 0; } } let outboxCursor = initOutboxCursor();` — module-init reads the current outbox.jsonl file size and treats that as the cursor's starting position. Pre-existing lines are now skipped per the spec. Inline comment block updated to call out the alignment and reference the §13.13.2 dedup masking that hid the impact previously. **Trade-off discipline**: this matches spec intent but means lines appended to outbox.jsonl while the bridge is dead will be lost on respawn. The spec assumes the agent only appends when the bridge is live; adopters needing queue-during-restart semantics can override (e.g., persist cursor across restarts) as an opt-in extension — recommended pattern documented in the inline comment. EG's own outer `EstreGenesis-maintenance` workspace runs a separate `collab/collab-client.cjs` with line-count-based cursor persistence as a stricter local choice; that file is not part of the public reference impl. **No protocol wire change** — this is a reference impl alignment, not a §13.x specification change. No `Constellation.md` body change. No `local-bridge.eux` change (spec already documented the correct behavior). No `local-bridge-and-watcher-NOTES.md` change (the bug was in `.cjs`, not in the spec NOTES). No plugin manifest change. No schema change. No renderer change. No seed lib change. **docs/promo catch-up**: `docs/index.html` hero badge `v2.5.42 → v2.5.43`; `docs/shared/data.js` meta `'v2.5.42' → 'v2.5.43'` + `shipCount: 58 → 59`; `README.md` top badge `v2.5.42 → v2.5.43` + `Current:` line rewritten (EN + KO) to describe the bridge fix + §13.13.2 dedup masking. **Scope discipline**: `constellation/reference/runtime/local-bridge.cjs` (~4 lines net change) + `CHANGELOG.md` (this entry, EN + KO) + `docs/index.html` hero badge + `docs/shared/data.js` meta + `README.md` top badge + Versioning Current line (EN + KO). User flagged that the v2.5.40 promo prose `"(canonical EG default localizes to plain Korean; adopters localize)"` reflected a real design problem — the schema default `button_label` is hardcoded Korean (`"뭔 소리야? 한국어로 번역해줘 (내가 알아들을 수 있는 말로)"`) and `trigger_phrases_md` default is Korean-only, with the v0.5.0 spec saying "adopters localize for non-Korean reader-bases SHOULD". This conflated *EG-the-project* (Korean) with *Hyperbrief-the-library* (a public module that ships to adopters in any language); the practical reality is that the skill (LLM composing the IR) already knows the user's prevailing conversation language and can populate the IR accordingly, so the schema's Korean default never needs to surface for non-Korean users in normal flow. Just say it plainly."`) / KO (`"뭔 소리야? 한국어로 번역해줘 (내가 알아들을 수 있는 말로)"`) / JA (`"何これ？私が分かる言葉で。"`), specifies mixed-language session handling (follow most recent prevailing-language signal), and clarifies that schema/renderer defaults are last-resort fallback for IR-direct-call / programmatic / test invocations only — in normal skill-driven flow this fallback never surfaces. The v0.4.0 status entry had carried "PreToolUse hook + MCP server **deferred to v0.4.1+**"; the MCP server landed at v0.4.2 (cut v2.5.28), but the PreToolUse hook stayed in the `hooks.json` Phase 1 placeholder through v0.5.0 → v0.5.1 → v0.5.2 as each cycle prioritized schema / cross-module integration / clean-install blocker fixes. v2.5.37 closes the carry with an advise-mode hook design (exit 0, never block) that adds a *silent-skip detection layer* over the existing model-invoked SKILL.md discipline. **Hook architecture** — three files under `plugins/hyperbrief/hooks/`: (1) `hooks.json` — Claude Code hook registration (PreToolUse `AskUserQuestion` + `Bash` + Stop `*`); (2) `trigger-advise.cjs` (~190 LoC, deps-0 except Node stdlib) — the PreToolUse wrapper, runs on every matching tool call with stdin = tool input JSON, applies the danger-list match for Bash (12 patterns: `git push` / `gh release` / `gh pr create|merge` / `npm publish` / `pnpm publish` / `yarn publish` / `kubectl apply|delete|create` / `docker push` / `terraform apply` / `gcloud …deploy` / `aws s3 cp|sync|update|deploy` / `curl -X POST|PUT|DELETE`), generates a `decision_id` matching the §1 pattern, then routes per the 4-way decision tree (Constellation detection + standalone preference); (3) `revisit-scan.cjs` (~85 LoC) — the Stop wrapper, scans `hyperbrief-ledger.jsonl` for `revisit_date ≤ today` (excluding rows with `outcome_actual` filled) and `.hyperbrief/pending-reviews/` for unreviewed placeholders, emits a single advisory line on either signal. **Review-queue routing** (the user-requested extension): on PreToolUse hook fire, the script detects whether Constellation is reachable (CONSTELLATION_WS_URL env set + a local outbox path exists at one of `$CONSTELLATION_OUTBOX_PATH`, `assets/collab/outbox.jsonl`, or `.constellation/outbox.jsonl`). If yes → append a `DECISION_REQUEST` envelope to the outbox as a *pending-review placeholder* (carries `decision_id`, `origin: "hyperbrief-hook"`, `pending: true`, `detected_tool`, `detected_intent`, `stage: "pending-review"`, `ack_tier_required: "decided"`); the local Constellation bridge relays the envelope to the board and the board's decisions/review-items panel surfaces it; stderr advise mentions the board surface explicitly. If no → check `auto_generate_review_doc` (env `HYPERBRIEF_AUTO_GENERATE_REVIEW_DOC=on|off|ask` or `.hyperbrief/config.json {auto_generate_review_doc: "on"|"off"|"ask"}`, default `"ask"`). When `"on"` → write a placeholder MD to `.hyperbrief/pending-reviews/<decision_id>.md` carrying detected tool + intent + raw tool input clipped to 4KB + next-step instructions; stderr advise mentions the file path. When `"ask"` (default) → stderr advise only + setup-hint pointing at the config knob. When `"off"` → simple stderr alert, no file. This 4-way design lets the hook function as a *deferred-review pipeline* — the user can defer decisions for later inspection rather than being forced into immediate-or-skip dichotomy at the alert moment, which composes cleanly with the §2.4 alert-fatigue circuit breaker. The pending → HyperbriefCard upgrade follows the same envelope-pair pattern Constellation §13.16.9 already carries (DECISION_REQUEST + paired HyperbriefCard by parentId; ack_tier='decided' on the Constellation MCP `a2a_wait_ack` side per v2.5.28). **`Hyperbrief.md §11.4` Hook-tier review queue (v0.5.3 — Claude Code plugin-tier discipline)** new sub-section ~60 lines: hook contract (advise mode invariants); 4-way review-queue routing with stderr message templates; "why advise mode (not hard-block)" rationale grounded in §2.4 alert-fatigue circuit breaker semantics; falsification triggers (10/day → matcher too broad; 0/week with samples accumulating → matcher too narrow or stderr propagation broken; 3+ revisits past date → notify-on-revisit opt-in candidate); cross-references to Constellation §13.16.9 / §13.16.10 + Hyperbrief §8. Cascades across all 6 seed tiers (Master + Lite + Compact × EN/KO).** Seed-lib cut. Bundle 007 M1 surfaced a 2-track tracking gap: the seed-version marker (e.g., `v2.4.1`, embedded in `AGENTS.md`) and the EG-release version (e.g., `v2.5.x`, advancing on every meaningful push per `feedback_release_versioning_cadence.md`) are independent — a release-only cut (e.g., Constellation `§13.x` patch, Hyperbrief module ship) does NOT bump the seed version, so a migrating adopter that checks only the seed marker may conclude "no delta" when substantial module/spec changes have landed. The fix is a Migration B Step 1 + Step 2 rewrite (Master tier full, Lite tier condensed, Compact tier 1-liner) that makes the dual-track expectation explicit. **Master tier (Master EN + Master KO)** — Step 1 expanded from one paragraph to a structured sub-section naming the two tracks ("seed version" vs "EG release version") + a "Check both markers before declaring a starting version" paragraph explaining the failure mode + cross-check sources (AGENTS.md seed marker + adoption manifest EG-release + upstream `CHANGELOG.md` HEAD) + revised user-question wording ("which EG release tag was current at that time?"). Step 2 prefaced with "List X for the starting **seed version** (table below), AND list Y for the starting **release version** (consult upstream `CHANGELOG.md` between the two release tags — typically a `git log <starting-tag>..HEAD --oneline -- CHANGELOG.md` against the EG repo, or just read the CHANGELOG entries between the two tags)" and the existing seed-delta table is now labeled "Seed-delta table" so readers know it's only one of the two tracks. **Lite tier (Lite EN + Lite KO)** — condensed equivalent: Step 1 carries the dual-track explanation in 2 sentences + cross-check instruction; Step 2 prefaced with the dual-track diff. **Compact tier (Compact EN + Compact KO)** — 1-liner extension at the start of Step 1 + 1-liner reframe of Step 2 ("diff capabilities (both tracks)"). **Frontmatter version markers** — all 6 tier headers bump `version: v2.4.1 → v2.4.2` + `date: 2026-05-31 → 2026-06-03` + status fragment `v2.4.2 = bundle 007 M1 reflection — Migration B Step 1/2 dual-track guidance` (Master) / condensed forms (Lite + Compact). **Why a seed bump (rather than just a CHANGELOG note)** — the change is to the seed body itself (Migration B procedure), not to a referenced module — adopters bootstrapping new projects from this seed cut get the dual-track guidance built into the Migration B section, not as an out-of-band CHANGELOG cross-reference. The seed-version marker was unchanged since v2.4.1 (2026-05-31) because the prior cuts (v2.5.0 through v2.5.34) were all release-track changes that did not touch the seed body — this is the first true seed-body change since v2.4.1, validating the 2-track separation that the change itself codifies. **Cross-tier consistency check passes** — the dual-track guidance is now present in all 6 tiers; the substance is identical (two tracks, cross-check both, ask user which EG release tag was current); the verbosity scales per tier (Master = full prose explanation, Lite = 2 sentences, Compact = 1 line). **Scope discipline**: 6 seed-tier files (Master EN + Master KO + Lite EN + Lite KO + Compact EN + Compact KO) — each gets Migration B Step 1 and Step 2 prefix updates + frontmatter version bump. Bundle 007 (Hyperbrief adoption dogfooding from a downstream adopter) surfaced a blocker: `ajv` 8.x default export is the draft-07 dialect, but `hyperbrief.schema.json` declares `"$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema"` — so `ajv.compile(schema)` throws `no schema with key or ref draft/2020-12/schema` on every IR, breaking the validation-on default code path entirely. The adopter could render only with `--skip-validate`; shipped packages installed via `npm install` could not validate at all. - **v2.5.22** (2026-06-02) — **constellation plugin v0.2.2 → v0.2.3: README "Infrastructure requirements" section added prominently for community-marketplace submission readiness; plugin manifest + marketplace description rewritten to disclose external-WS-server dependency upfront.** Plugin documentation patch — `plugins/constellation/README.md` gains a new prominent ⚠ section between the intro paragraph and "What this plugin gives you", spelling out the three runtime requirements (WS server at `CONSTELLATION_WS_URL`; state file at `CONSTELLATION_STATE_PATH`; role-keyed auth via `CONSTELLATION_TOKEN` / `_UPSTREAM_KEY` / `_COLLAB_KEY`), explaining what the plugin does WITHOUT a running server (loads clean, skills are docs-only, hook degrades gracefully, MCP tool calls fail with connection errors), and explaining why the architecture chooses external infra over a bundled default server (Constellation is a peer-coordination layer; the WS server holds shared state across agents, so bundling a single-process default server would defeat the multi-agent purpose). The README also adds a `What's in v0.2.3` and a backfilled `What's in v0.2.2` section (the v0.2.2 README sync from v2.5.20 was bundle-only and did not include a release-notes section in the README itself). Anthropic does not publish an explicit policy on plugins with external infrastructure dependencies, but the official `claude-plugins-official` marketplace already lists multiple precedents (Airtable, MongoDB, PostgreSQL, GitHub, Stripe — all of which connect to user-managed accounts / services / databases external to the plugin install), and the Claude Code MCP documentation explicitly endorses remote MCP servers (HTTP / SSE / WebSocket) as a standard supported transport. The conclusion is that infrastructure-dependent plugins are accepted; the submission-readiness work is therefore (a) explicit upfront disclosure in README + marketplace description and (b) clear graceful-degradation messaging — both of which v0.2.3 delivers. **Scope discipline**: plugin documentation + manifest version bumps only. Discriminator is the owner of the agent-layer commitment signal, not the implementation language; same failure mode applies regardless of layer. **§13.9.1 AgentHello opt-in broadcast presence** — strict required handshake is `SERVER_HELLO` + `HELLO`; `AgentHello` is opt-in broadcast presence that (a) declares display metadata and (b) triggers receiver-bridge `OnboardAck` auto-emit. Adopters MAY skip when broadcast presence is undesirable (headless / stealth / telemetry-only / ephemeral debug); skipping yields a working connection without display metadata or auto-OnboardAck-driven worker standby. Discipline: when sent, MUST follow §2 step 3 wire shape; for `upstream` / `collab` MUST be broadcast (no specific `targetAgentId`); MUST NOT be used as a directed DM to `main-agent` (that misuse drives the alias-confusion failure mode below). Adopters MAY operate aliases (e.g., treat `main-agent` placeholder as an alias for their actual canonical id) handled at the adapter layer. Adopter discipline: inbound target-alias SHOULD route to canonical; inbound source-alias + target-canonical MUST be treated as self-loop and dropped (recursive-wake prevention); outbound traffic MUST stamp canonical id (not alias) at `agentId` / `source`; dashboards SHOULD render `AgentList` rows by canonical id (alias is implementation detail). Named failure mode prevented: **alias-confusion** — an adapter treating `main-agent` as a separate peer, sending `AgentHello` as DM to it, receiving auto-`OnboardAck` for an identity that does not exist, with the live-board UI rendering the same agent twice (canonical + alias) and no error surface. **Scope discipline**: spec-body patch only (~3 paragraphs in §13.13 + two new sub-sections in §13.9 + frontmatter version bump + status string). - **v2.5.17** (2026-06-02) — **Constellation `§13.13.2` v0.4 → v0.5 spec patch — bridge inbox-append commitment + `delivered-persist` ack subtier (eliminates false-positive `RelayUnreachable{commitment-ack-absent}`).** Spec-body patch — `Constellation.md` §13.13.2 sub-section header bumped from `(v0.4 draft)` to `(v0.5)` + three new paragraphs (g) bridge inbox-append commitment + (h) tier-semantics vocabulary table + (i) migration path v0.4 → v0.5. Wire format unchanged (optional `tier` field added to `AckProcessed.value`, back-compatible). **Trigger** — 2026-06-02 dogfood: relay RRP §13.13.2 v0.4 hub adoption immediately after v2.5.15 ship surfaced a false-positive class — a normal `Ack` from EG → main was redelivered 3× → `RelayUnreachable{commitment-ack-absent}` despite the body having reached main's inbox file on the first attempt, because main's agent layer did not happen to emit a commitment-tier `AckProcessed` for it (agent idle / processing unrelated work). Main paused redelivery to OFF gate (`RELAY_REDELIVERY=off`) + proposed v0.5: bridge emits the commitment ack on its own authority immediately after inbox-append, since the bridge owns the persistence guarantee and the agent layer's commitment is properly an *outcome* signal not a *delivery* signal. EG agreed with all five arguments (false-positive removal · bridge always alive · v0.4 LRU dedup composes · agent layer keeps application-tier ack only · inbox-append IS the at-least-once anchor); main implemented main bridge v0.5 + restarted (PID 437484) + granted EG autonomous authority to ship spec patch + EG-side reference impl. **§13.13.2 (g) Bridge inbox-append commitment** — codifies the v0.5 contract: every successful inbound `CUSTOM` body that the recipient's bridge appends to its inbox file MUST be followed within milliseconds by `AckProcessed { ackFor: msgId, tier: "delivered-persist" }` emitted to the sender. Bridge does NOT wait for agent layer to read or process; the moment the body is durably persisted, the bridge has fulfilled its half of the at-least-once contract. Server treats `tier:"delivered-persist"` as the canonical pending-queue clear trigger, semantically equivalent to v0.4's commitment-tier ack but emitted by the transport layer that actually owns the persistence guarantee. **§13.13.2 (h) Tier semantics** — v0.5 distinguishes three named tiers with explicit emitter/trigger/pending-clear columns: `delivered` (server-emitted, wire received, no pending clear) · `delivered-persist` (bridge-emitted, inbox-append complete, canonical pending clear) · `commitment` (agent-emitted, body surfaced into working context, redundant after `delivered-persist`). Application-tier outcomes (`Report` / `DONE` / `BLOCKED` per §13.13) live on a separate outcome dimension; v0.4 `AckProcessed` without `tier` field is interpreted as `commitment` for back-compat (a v0.4 receiver paired with v0.5 server continues to operate at v0.4 semantics, including the false-positive class — the escape requires the v0.5 *bridge*). **§13.13.2 (i) Migration path** — per-component update: server gains "delivered-persist clears pending entry" rule (additive over v0.4 commitment-tier clear) + optional per-target `RELAY_REDELIVERY=off` gate (operators disable redelivery while v0.5 bridges roll out); bridge adds inbox-append hook with immediate `delivered-persist` emit (composes with v0.4 §13.13.2(c) LRU dedup — duplicates still emit `AckProcessed{ackFor, dedupHit:true}` without inbox-append, so no `delivered-persist` for duplicates); agent unchanged (mechanism is bridge-layer, invisible to agent code). **Empirical validation** — 2026-06-02 dogfood with main-EG bidirectional: main's bridge added the hook + restart (PID 437484) + the next EG → main envelope cleared pending in <1s without redelivery or `RelayUnreachable`. EG-side reference impl (the v2.5.18 ship) is the EG bridge complement. **Scope discipline**: spec-body patch only (~3 paragraphs added to §13.13.2 sub-section + header version bump + frontmatter). - **v2.5.15** (2026-06-02) — **Constellation `§13.13.2` v0.4 reference implementation — server pending queue + redelivery scheduler + RelayUnreachable emit + bridge LRU dedup with `dedupHit:true` AckProcessed.** Reference-runtime patch — `constellation/reference/runtime/server.cjs` + `constellation/reference/runtime/local-bridge.cjs`. Constellation.md body unchanged (the §13.13.2 contract codified in v2.5.11 is the spec; this version is its reference implementation per the §13.13.2 Phase 2 deferred-list). Seed lib unchanged. Triggered by user instruction ("바로 진행하지?"). **server.cjs additions** (`constellation/reference/runtime/server.cjs` ~lines 155-200 + relay branch): **(a) Pending queue** — `_relayPending` Map keyed by `targetAgentId`, FIFO per-target with cap `RELAY_PENDING_MAX=256` (env-overridable). Each entry `{ msgId, payload, firstAt, attempts, hasEmbeddedAttachment }`. Entries register on the relay branch whenever `wsIsAckable(msg)` returns true AND the target is connected — same gate as the transport-tier `Ack delivered` emit; the v0.3 baseline already filtered ack/ping/telemetry out of the pending track. **(b) Commitment-tier clear on AckProcessed** — when a `CUSTOM/AckProcessed` envelope is relayed with `value.ackFor` matching a pending entry's msgId AND a `targetAgentId` matching the original target, `_relayPendingClear(tgt, ackFor)` removes the entry. This is the key inversion vs v0.3: pending is cleared by commitment-tier ack (agent layer), NOT by transport-tier `Ack delivered` (server layer). **(c) Redelivery scheduler** — `setInterval(_relayScheduleTick, 10*1000)` scans pending entries every 10s; an entry past `RELAY_THRESHOLD_MS` (default 30s dogfood / 5min prod — env-overridable) AND recipient AgentList-present AND attempts < max → redeliver via `d.send(payload)` + increment attempts + reset firstAt. Recipient-absent → defer redelivery until reconnect. Max-attempts hit → emit `RelayUnreachable { msgId, targetAgentId, attemptCount, lastError }` to the **sender** (not broadcast — only the sender needs to know its message did not stick) + clear pending entry. The sender then escalates to human review per §13.13 application-tier ladder. **(d) §13.11 rule 5 attachment-aware throttle** — entries carrying `value.attachments[]` with any `source: "embedded"` (or any `dataUrl` field) attachment use `Math.ceil(max_attempts / 2)` as the effective cap (default 3 → 2 for embedded). Duplicate large payload redelivery is bandwidth-expensive + the receiver's msgId dedup catches it on first redelivery anyway; the throttle is the cost-asymmetry response. **(e) Scheduler unref'd** (`.unref()`) — does not keep the Node event loop alive past server shutdown. **local-bridge.cjs additions** (`constellation/reference/runtime/local-bridge.cjs` ~lines 75-104): **(f) LRU dedup with TTL** — `_seenMsgIds` upgraded from unbounded `Set` to `Map(msgId → seen-ts)` with `_SEEN_LRU_MAX=1024` entries + `_SEEN_TTL_MS=1h` per §13.13.2 v0.4 provisional defaults. `_dedupCheck(msgId)` performs TTL evict from oldest (Map insertion-order iteration is JS spec) + LRU evict on cap + insert/refresh. Returns true on duplicate. **(g) `dedupHit: true` AckProcessed emit** — when `_dedupCheck` returns true, the bridge emits `CUSTOM/AckProcessed { ackFor: <msgId>, dedupHit: true }` targeted at the original sender agent (`m.agentId || m.value.agentId`) + discards the body (no inbox.jsonl append, no agent layer surface). The sender's server-side `_relayPending` entry then clears via path (b) above. Without `dedupHit` emit, redelivery would loop indefinitely until max-attempts (RelayUnreachable false-alarm); with `dedupHit` emit, redelivery is server-side mechanic invisible to the agent layer (correct §13.13.2 semantic). **Env-overridable knobs**: `RELAY_PENDING_MAX` (default 256) · `RELAY_THRESHOLD_MS` (default 30000 = 30s; prod adopters set to 300000 = 5min) · `RELAY_MAX_ATTEMPTS` (default 3). Scheduler scan interval is hardcoded at 10s (sub-threshold; tunable in code). **What v2.5.15 does NOT add** (still §13.13.2 Phase 3 candidates): durable pending queue (in-memory only; server restart loses pending state — acceptable for dogfood, prod adopters add persistence) · cross-server pending state (single-server scope) · telemetry sink for redelivery/dedup-hit/RelayUnreachable rate calibration (logged via `console.warn` only) · per-target backpressure (a slow recipient just accumulates pending up to cap then FIFO-evicts oldest). **Composition tested**: PR #4/PR #5 trace would now also clear server pending on the manual fast-path PRMergeAck (which is application-tier, not commitment) — Phase 3 may add explicit application-tier pending clear OR rely on max-attempts timeout. For now, application-tier outcomes do NOT auto-clear pending (only commitment-tier does); long-running tasks should emit AckProcessed at acceptance time. **Scope discipline**: reference-runtime patch only (~70 lines added to server.cjs + ~25 lines added to local-bridge.cjs). Chunked transfer (`ArtifactManifest`/`ArtifactChunk`/`ArtifactComplete`) is independently idempotent at chunk level + does NOT participate in msgId pending queue at chunk granularity. **(f) Composition with broker-forward workaround** — the workaround codified in `memory/feedback_a2a_relay_reliability.md` (extract from main `ws-history/<sender-agentId>.jsonl` and forward to recipient) remains a valid manual escalation path even after v0.4 ships, for cases where pending queue exceeds cap or recipient stays disconnected past `RelayUnreachable`. The hardened version probes the system for a watcher process matching the watcher-script basename via `pgrep -f` (POSIX) with `tasklist /V /FO CSV` fallback (Windows); if alive → skip spawn (no leak); if neither tool is available (bare Windows without git-bash) → skip spawn with the "agent-side rearm is canonical" log line (cost-asymmetry argument inverted — a false-positive skip costs nothing because the agent's turn-end rearm runs anyway, while a false-positive spawn-leak costs a background process per turn). **Hardening 2 — cursor advance on meaningful in REARM mode (infinite-loop prevention)**: the original `--rearm` mode exited 2 when meaningful inbound was found but did NOT advance the cursor, so the next turn-close re-detected the same meaningful and exit-2'd again, repeating indefinitely. The hardened version ADVANCES the cursor before exit 2 — the meaningful is logged once (stderr → agent's next-turn input surface), subsequent probes start clean. The agent's §13.16.6 element 1 turn-start probe is the canonical inspection point; the Stop hook's role is LOG + advance, not perpetual block. - **v2.5.5** (2026-06-01) — **Constellation `§13.16.12` new sub-section — Dashboard render patterns (6 protocol-tier abstractions from cycle_b track-2 raw cp #1).** Constellation patch — body-only augmentation, no wire-format change, no seed cascade. Frontmatter `version: v2.3.12 → v2.3.13`. New §13.16.12 inserted between §13.16.11 (KEY-MGMT kind-enum SSoT) and §13.17 (main-chat structured-choice ban), codifying six dashboard-render patterns as tier-1 SSoT discipline distilled from the cycle_b track-2 reference consolidation (six newer patterns surfaced through a single hub multi-fix commit on 2026-06-01, in addition to the five prior patterns already captured in `constellation/reference/docs/dashboard-render-patterns.md` v2.5.1). **Why a new sub-section, not just an update to `dashboard-render-patterns.md`**: the reference doc is the *render-tier companion* (renderer implementer's manual — file paths, function names, CSS selectors), while §13.16.12 is the *protocol-tier abstraction* (the *invariant* a renderer must satisfy regardless of stack). An adopter building a non-vanilla dashboard (React, Vue, Svelte, native) reads §13.16.12 for the contract and the reference doc for the vanilla-DOM concrete implementation. **The six patterns**: (1) **Collapse indicator: glyph unification + CSS rotation discipline** — single glyph rotated via `transform: rotate()` (canonical: `textContent="◀"` constant + `.expanded { transform: rotate(-90deg); transition .15s }`), NOT a `▾ / ◀` glyph swap pair (which produces 1-2 px visual jitter on every toggle from per-glyph metric mismatch — observable as "the row twitches"); orthogonal to the `[hidden]` CSS pitfall already captured in `dashboard-render-patterns.md §3`. (2) **Date-line divider: client-tz day-boundary insertion + sticky positioning** — day computed from `row.timestamp` (epoch ms, client-side `new Date(epoch)`) NEVER from wire-format ISO string (the wire string carries sender's tz; the divider must reflect the *viewer's* local-day boundary); `position: sticky; top: 0` with sticky-top offset accounting for chat-panel header height (not page header); locale-dependent visual canonical (`오늘 / 어제 / YYYY-MM-DD` Korean, `Today / Yesterday / YYYY-MM-DD` English) with `~ ~` decorators via `::before` / `::after` pseudo-elements (NOT literal DOM characters — keeps the divider text programmatically accessible). Composes with §13.11.3 rule 3 (server stamps `msg.timestamp = Date.now()` if absent; dashboard uses that epoch). (3) **A2A attachment chip: mime detection + preview + graceful localPath** — attachment metadata renders as inline chip inside message card body (NOT separate row beneath); mime-icon glyph + filename + size + (preview | download) triggers; preview/download MUST handle both wire shapes: `dataUrl`/`url` present → inline modal renders, OR only `localPath` present → chip renders gracefully with localPath as informational metadata + "local file, not transported" indicator (NEVER an error or broken-link icon — targetless / metadata-only attachments are a common emit pattern where the sender means "here's a file I have, name and check it" rather than "here's a file I'm transmitting"). Composes with §13.13: an `AckProcessed` on an attachment message means the recipient has *surfaced* the metadata, NOT that the recipient has downloaded the localPath resource. (4) **Closed-session connection indicator: present-set based color dot** — each agent row's connection indicator dot color reflects present membership in live `AgentList` (green `●` present, gray `●` absent — history-only); updates on every `AgentList` push (§13.9 handshake group); tooltip surfaces precise connection state with local-tz timestamp (composes with Pattern 2's client-local rendering); composes with §13.13 — a `delivered` ack to a gray-dot agent is wire suspect (recipient currently offline), dashboard MAY surface inline warning rather than escalating silently to commitment-tier wait. (5) **Upstream tab re-exposure: present-set sweep, not just delta** — auto-re-expose logic MUST trigger on every `AgentList` push where the agent is `present`, not only on `absent → present` delta. Rationale: long-lived upstream peers stay continuously connected and never produce an `absent → present` delta after initial join; if the operator collapses the tab mid-conversation, the tab stays collapsed forever even though the agent is actively producing messages. Discipline: on every `AgentList`, for each present agent, if the tab is currently `hidden`, un-hide it. The sweep is idempotent (re-exposing an already-visible tab is a no-op). Composes with §13.16.9 v2.5.2 — `AgentList` is in the handshake group so the watcher correctly does NOT wake on each push, but the dashboard MUST still re-evaluate tab visibility regardless of watcher-wake intent. (6) **Upstream A2A classification (receiver-side): source-set-agnostic detection + text relay fallback** — receiver-side A2A-intent detection MUST use the negation form of §13.11.3 rule 2: `source !== "user" && source !== "board" && targetAgentId && targetAgentId !== self`. CRITICALLY, MUST NOT use the positive-set form `source === "agent"` because upstream peer agents emit `source = <their-agentId>` (nonstandard but conformant); the positive-set check silently false-negatives ALL upstream A2A traffic. The negation form is portable across all emitter variants. **Text relay fallback** (second half of pattern): the server's outbound routing (§13.16.9 routing decision tree) MUST relay target-unspecified TEXT_MESSAGE envelopes to `wsPrimary` (main A2A path) when target-unspecified TEXT_MESSAGE is A2A-intent — the fail-safe-default-A2A-intent branch (fourth branch of the tree) MUST cover TEXT_MESSAGE name too, not just CUSTOM (otherwise upstream agents emitting raw text without CUSTOM wrap silently drop on server-side normalization). Composes with §13.11.3 rule 1 (channel `type` normalization handles producer-side defect; this pattern handles router-side defect independently). **Composition with `dashboard-render-patterns.md`**: the reference doc carries concrete render-tier patterns (function names, CSS selectors, file paths in vanilla-DOM master copy); §13.16.12 carries the protocol-tier discipline. The reference doc's eight sections correspond to §13.16.12's six patterns plus two prior-cycle patterns (§2 row interaction + §4 board render card form, already absorbed at protocol tier through §13.16.9 + §13.11.3 in v2.5.1). **Scope discipline**: Constellation.md body augmentation only (one new sub-section ~110 lines). Wire format unchanged (Patterns 1-5 are render-tier behavior; Pattern 6 codifies receiver-side detection rule + routing tree branch that v2.5.1 §13.16.9 already documented). `dashboard-render-patterns.md` unchanged in v2.5.5 — continues as renderer's concrete manual. Seed lib unchanged. Hub mirror via A2A PR #3 is a separate follow-up. Per `feedback_release_versioning_cadence.md` — meaningful protocol body augmentation cut, not catch-up.

- **v2.5.2** (2026-06-01) — **Constellation §13.11 receiver text synthesize SHOULD + §13.13 3-tier ack mapping + §13.16.9 4-group classification + §13.16.10 cycle-end probe extension.** Constellation patch — body-only augmentations across four §13.x sub-sections, no wire-format change, no seed cascade. Frontmatter `version: v2.3.11 → v2.3.12`. **§13.11 envelope augmentation (rule 4 — receiver text synthesize SHOULD)**: codifies the agent/render-layer affordance discipline. When a targeted `CUSTOM` arrives with `targetAgentId === self` but no plain `text` field in `value`, the receiver (LLM turn, dashboard render layer, downstream worker) SHOULD synthesize a text representation from the envelope's structured metadata for display or LLM-turn ingestion. Canonical synthesize shape: `<name> from <agentId> (msgId=<msgId>, threadId=<threadId>): <JSON.stringify(value)>`. The discipline is SHOULD for renderers + LLM turn ingest paths and MAY for downstream workers that consume the structured `value` directly. The wire-layer rule is unchanged — `{ name, value, targetAgentId? }` remains the minimal carrier shape; `text` is optional and absence does not invalidate the envelope. Producers MUST NOT be required to author a `text` field redundant with `value`. Cross-link to `constellation/reference/docs/dashboard-render-patterns.md §4 board render card form` (the dashboard's collapsible JSON body + envelope summary card is the dashboard-render-layer instance of this synthesize discipline). **§13.13 explicit 3-tier ack name-to-tier mapping**: codifies the previously-implicit tier semantics behind the §13.13 ack vocabulary as a named table. Three tiers: **transport** (`Ack` · `AckProcessed`-as-wire-mechanic · `AckCumulative` · `AckPolicyUpdate` · `Ping` · `Pong` — the carrier confirms wire/server/bridge delivery; no semantic guarantee about agent-side processing); **commitment** (`AckProcessed`-as-semantic — the recipient agent has read and intends to act, distinct from delivered); **application** (`Report` · `DONE` · `BLOCKED` · `NEEDS_HUMAN` · domain-specific outcome names — the agent has completed the action and reports the outcome). `AckProcessed` appears in both transport and commitment because the wire mechanic IS transport (an ack frame returns) but the semantic IS commitment (the agent — not the bridge — asserts it has surfaced the inbound). Discriminator: `Ack` = "delivered to inbox"; `AckProcessed` = "agent has surfaced this into its working context". **Escalation ladder** (the absence-of-tier-N → probe-tier-N → next-tier sequence): absence of transport-tier ack → wire suspect (§4 watchdog territory, NOT A2A retry); absence of commitment-tier → recipient slow/absorbed (`Ping` probe per §13.13); absence of application-tier → recipient stuck (surface to human via board `decisions` panel; do NOT autonomous-retry). The ordering matters — an adopter who escalates from transport directly to human review skips the probe layer that distinguishes "wire dead" from "agent slow"; an adopter who treats `Ack` as "done" misses the commitment-vs-application distinction the retry tree depends on. **§13.16.9 4-group classification** (documentation-side SSoT for downstream Constellation adopters): expands the prior 2-group + transport-tier shape to a 4-group classification naming previously-implicit groups as first-class siblings of board-directed and A2A-intent. **transport** (`Ack` · `AckProcessed` · `AckCumulative` · `AckPolicyUpdate` · `Ping` · `Pong` — server-side relay-only-or-relay-skip per reference impl server.cjs L849 area; no agent-side wake); **liveness** (`Heartbeat` · `PersistentAdapterSmoke` · `Typing` — bridge/server transient signals; server relay-skip; no board chat record; agent layer ignores); **handshake** (`AgentHello` · `OnboardAck` · `AgentList` · `History` — §13.9 onboarding family; bridge auto-`OnboardAck` handles inbound automatically; agent layer does NOT wake on this group); **notice** (`ServerNotice` — broadcast-class via `wsToAll` per server L828 area; informational); **board-directed UX residual** (`Status` · `UserPromptAccepted` · `ConnectionRestored` · `MainChanged` · `EditMessage` · `WorkerInboxReceived` — dashboard UX-only); **A2A-intent existing** (`Report` · `Delegate` · `WorkerReport` · `WorkerAck` · `Handoff`* · `Command` · `UserPrompt` · `BlockerManifest` · `BlockerNudge` · `PR`* · `Deadlock`* · `Review`* · `ReviewSLAAck` · `PreemptRequest` · `MediationProposal` · `MediationAck` · `EscalationRequest` — meaningful filter target). **Reclassifications**: `AgentHello` moves from A2A-intent meaningful filter to handshake group (bridge auto-`OnboardAck` handles, agent does not wake — removes the unnecessary watcher wake per peer connect); `Heartbeat` / `PersistentAdapterSmoke` / `Typing` move from board-directed UX to liveness (aligns documentation with server relay-skip behavior); `AgentList` / `History` / `OnboardAck` consolidate into handshake group alongside `AgentHello` (onboarding-family coherence). **Meaningful filter for §13.16.6 watcher** (updated cross-reference): meaningful = A2A-intent group ONLY. The other four groups (transport + liveness + handshake + notice + board-directed UX residual) are ALL noise from the watcher's perspective. **Hub-side `_BOARD_DIRECTED` 12-name backward-compat preservation**: the post-v2.4.17 reference server.cjs `_BOARD_DIRECTED` constant carries the original 12-name set unchanged; the 4-group reclassification is documentation-side. Adopters reimplementing the routing decision tree from the SSoT MAY use the 4-group form directly; back-compat behavior preserved for adopters pinned to the hub-side 12-name implementation. **§13.16.10 cycle-end + user-facing emit-direct probe extension**: extends the §13.16.10 pre-send probe-then-inspect-or-abort discipline (which fires before each outbound A2A emit) to cover the *cycle-end user-facing assistant text emit*. The defect: pre-send probe runs before each outbound A2A emit, but does NOT run before the user-facing assistant text emit at cycle-end. If meaningful inbound arrives between the last outbound A2A emit and the cycle-end user-text emit, the agent silently misses it — the next watcher WAKE catches it but the user-facing response is already framed without the new context. **The extension** (two rules added to §13.16.10; the existing outbound-A2A four-step shape unchanged): (1) **Cycle-end final cursor-tail probe** — just before the user-facing assistant text emits, the agent MUST run a final cursor-tail probe (same shape as pre-send probe, A2A-intent allowlist filter); if meaningful inbound is found, revise the in-progress response OR explicitly note the catch + next-cycle handling; (2) **Post-emit watcher rearm** — turn-end MUST include a watcher rearm (restates §13.16.6 element 2 in the §13.16.10 cycle-end context); unconditional spawn per the cost-asymmetry argument (false-positive = one task slot, false-negative = silent-stall class). **Pattern name**: "cycle-end probe + watcher rearm" (companion to "pre-send probe-then-inspect-or-abort"). **Failure-mode incident anchor**: 2 missed-inbound incidents on 2026-06-01, both downstream of cycle-end probe omission; corrective surface was main-side reminders at next user message. **memory `feedback_pre_send_inbound_check.md` augmentation**: new "Cycle-end probe (v2.5.2 extension)" section with the rule + watcher-rearm pair + worked-example incident (cycle_b v2.5.1 ship-result emit where main-upstream protocol_update_proposal arrived during response composition and was missed until next user message) + composition with §13.16.6 element 1 / §13.16.10 outbound surface / new cycle-end surface (three disjoint probe windows: pre-turn-boundary / mid-turn-outbound / post-emit-pre-close). MEMORY.md index entry updated to mention the cycle-end extension. **Claude Code Stop hook config artifact** at `assets/scripts/STOP-HOOK-CONFIG.md` (project-scope, gitignored under `/assets/`): codifies the harness-level mechanization — every turn-close runs `node assets/scripts/pre-send-probe.cjs --rearm` automatically. Helper script `pre-send-probe.cjs` augmented with `--rearm` flag (cycle-end probe + watcher rearm + cursor file management); applies the §13.16.9 v2.5.2 4-group allowlist (meaningful = A2A-intent only). Recommended config snippet in `.claude/settings.local.json` (gitignored) — operator applies via `/config` or `update-config` skill. **Scope discipline**: Constellation.md body augmentation + memory feedback + Stop hook config artifact (gitignored). Seed library unchanged (anchor references only). Wire format unchanged. Hub-side `_BOARD_DIRECTED` 12-name implementation preserved (documentation-side reclassification only — downstream Constellation adopters use the 4-group SSoT for new implementations; existing implementations remain back-compatible). Per `feedback_release_versioning_cadence.md` — in-flight patch tag cut, not catch-up.
- **v2.5.1** (2026-06-01) — **Constellation track-2 reference consolidation (11 patterns): `Constellation.md` §13.11 envelope + §13.16.9 routing decision tree + §13.16.11 KEY-MGMT augmentations + new `constellation/reference/docs/dashboard-render-patterns.md` reference doc.** Constellation patch — track-2 consolidation of 11 dashboard-render-adjacent patterns surfaced through upstream main commits over 2026-05~06 dogfood (5 prior surfaced patterns + 6 newer surfaced patterns from a single multi-fix commit). Frontmatter `version: v2.3.10 → v2.3.11`. **Tier-1 protocol body augmentations** (`Constellation.md`): (a) **§13.11.3 new sub-section — envelope normalization and client-local render**: three independent server-/receiver-side normalization rules at the envelope layer — rule 1 **channel `type` normalization** (server MUST stamp `type:"CUSTOM"` on outbound when sender omits; agents may emit minimal `{ name, value, targetAgentId? }` carriers and rely on server normalization; without this, dashboard render falls back to TEXT_MESSAGE and JSON leaks into chat panel); rule 2 **A2A-intent detection rule** (source-set-agnostic — `source !== "user" && source !== "board" && targetAgentId && targetAgentId !== self`; CRITICALLY `source` is NOT fixed at `"agent"` because upstream agents may emit `source = <their-agentId>`, a nonstandard but conformant source value; the positive-set assumption `source === "agent"` silently false-negatives all upstream A2A traffic — the negation pattern is portable across emitter variants); rule 3 **timestamp obligation + client-local render** (server MUST stamp `msg.timestamp = Date.now()` epoch ms if absent; dashboard render MUST use `new Date(epoch).toTimeString()` for client-local tz display, NEVER the wire-format ISO string verbatim which would show sender's tz and confuse multi-tz teams). Composition: rules 1+3 server-side; rule 2 receiver-side; all three independent failure modes. (b) **§13.16.9 routing decision tree** appended: the canonical form `(has targetAgentId?) → route to that agent; (no targetAgentId? AND name ∈ board-directed) → wsToBoards only (no wsPrimaryAgent fallback); (no targetAgentId? AND name ∈ A2A-intent) → wsPrimaryAgent + optional board mirror; (no targetAgentId? AND unknown) → fail-safe default A2A-intent`. References the post-v2.4.17 L867 routing branch as canonical implementation. The tree composes with §13.11.3 rule 1 (`type` normalization runs first; then routing decision tree); both steps part of the same `wsNormalize` + `wsRoute` outbound path. (c) **§13.16.11 KEY-MGMT new sub-section — kind-enum SSoT**: unified key-management contract codifying the `kind` enum (`collab` | `upstream` | `local-key`) carried on every key-bearing envelope. Four SSoT surfaces: server `keyStore` stamps `kind` on every entry; `KeyList` broadcast carries `kind` per entry; `HELLO.meta` echoes resolved `kind` for self-classification; dashboard key-management modal renders `kind`-badge per entry. Composition: §13.16.9 routing should include key-management names in board-directed allowlist; §13.14 redaction discipline — `kind` enum is vocabulary (not sensitive), only key values (`ck-…` / `uk-…` suffixes) are environment-specific credentials. Wire shapes preserved — `kind` is an additional top-level field, server-stamped on issuance, mandatory on `KeyList` entries, optional on `HELLO.meta`. **Tier-2 dashboard render policy** (new file `constellation/reference/docs/dashboard-render-patterns.md`, ~3902 words / ~26.8 KB, 8 sections): companion document covering render-side patterns above the wire — §1 introduction (scope: render-tier patterns surfaced through 2026-05~06 dogfood; raw TEXT fallback when type-omitted = symptom of §13.11.3 rule 1 server-side defect); §5 date-line divider (insert at midnight crossing in chronological stream; `position: sticky; top: <header-height>` keeps most-recent date label visible during scroll; `오늘 / 어제 / YYYY-MM-DD` text per locale with `~ ~` decorators; sticky offset must account for chat-panel header height not just page header); §6 A2A attachment chip (mime-icon emoji glyph + filename + size + preview/download triggers, rendered inside card body not as separate row — keeps attachment-message association visible; - **v2.5.0** (2026-06-01) — **Superscalar.md v0.3 — §2 lane-class-aware `issue_width` cap split (read vs write) + §2 policy cap vs runtime concurrency ceiling sub-section + §5 lane-class-differentiated adoption thresholds + §11 Entry 05 (downstream Stage 1 dogfooding n=7).** Minor release — Superscalar.md policy-doc body change + Compact + Master seed cascade. Reflects a downstream adopter's Stage 1 dogfooding bundle (real-time chat-service microservices, full seed adoption incl. Superscalar + Constellation, Burst pace mode `issue_width` cap 6, n=7 retired lanes over ~3 days, case-based ledger) — proposal filed at `_proposals/005_2026-06-01_superscalar-dogfooding-stage1/`. **§2 cap split**: a single `issue_width` formula previously covered all lane classes uniformly; v0.3 splits it into `issue_width_write = min(effort_band, pace_mode_cap, Little's-Law, Kanban-WIP, autonomy_available_workers)` and `issue_width_read = min(effort_band, runtime_concurrency_ceiling, autonomy_available_workers)`. The two terms dropped from the read class (Little's Law, Kanban WIP) only model retire-merge contention that read-only lanes structurally don't have — no store buffer, no retire-merge ordering, no WAW hazard, disposable on synthesis. Read-only / analysis lanes (subagent context sweeps, workflow read fan-outs, telemetry reads) carry no irreversible side effects and inherit the read/write boundary §3 already draws for the irreversibility barrier (read/analyze default-allowed; write/deploy/send retire-gated). **§2 new sub-section — policy cap vs runtime concurrency ceiling**: the `issue_width_*` caps are policy bounds; the runtime concurrency ceiling (e.g. workflow's `min(16, cores − 2)` per workflow; harness max parallel tool calls for agent-tool fan-outs) is a separate physical bound. Relationship: `effective_concurrent_lanes = min(policy_cap, runtime_ceiling)`. For workflow-based read fan-outs the runtime ceiling typically dominates; for agent-tool-based fan-outs the policy cap typically dominates. `issue_width_write` is a hard policy bound (exceeding it is a policy violation regardless of runtime headroom — retire-merge contention scales with concurrent writes); `issue_width_read` is a soft preference subject to the runtime ceiling above it (a read-only fan-out that exceeds `issue_width_read` but stays under `runtime_concurrency_ceiling` is not a policy violation, at most a calibration signal). **§5 adoption-threshold lane-class differentiation**: the threshold values are unchanged from prior versions; what is new is which lane class each threshold binds. `merge-conflict rate > 15% → issue_width_write -= 2` applies to write lanes only (read-only lanes have no merge surface, conflict = NA). `speculative accuracy < 60% → spec off` · `concurrent token cost vs in-order > 3× → cap re-tune` · `FM-1.3 detection ≥ 1/session → guard up` apply symmetrically (cross-cutting concerns, not retire-merge contention). **§11 Entry 05 added**: downstream Stage 1 dogfooding n=7 over ~3 days. Case mix = 1 board-worker A2A · 5 read-only research subagents · 1 workflow fan-out (case 7 = 7 reader lanes, exceeded policy cap 6 with zero downside — the empirical anchor for the §2 cap split). Confirmations: latency-hiding thesis · speculation off-by-default 0/7 · MAST FM-1.3 = 0 · in-order retire held. §5 readout: all thresholds green at n=7 (case 7's cap-exceed was a read-only lane, conflict = NA, does not count against the merge-conflict signal — empirical confirmation of the §5 lane-class differentiation). Unexercised surface: worktree-isolation 0/7 · speculation 0/7 · wide write fan-out 0. Relation to Entry 04: complementary, not redundant (Entry 04 varied in-lane depth at fixed width below cap; Entry 05 varies cross-lane fan-out above cap on read class). Outcome: P1 (lane-class cap asymmetry, actionable) + R1 (cap split adopted in §2/§5) + R2 (policy/runtime relationship clarified in §2) all reflected upstream. **Seed cascade**: Master EN/KO § Execution Scheduling — `### The invariant — issue_width formula` body updated to the lane-class-aware split + policy/runtime ceiling note (Master embeds the formula body, not just an anchor); Compact EN/KO Principle #15 inline formula expanded to the lane-class form with §5 binding note; Lite EN/KO unchanged (Lite tier references `Superscalar.md` by anchor only, no formula body). Bootstrap Phase 0 boilerplate unchanged (lane class is an internal mechanic; the user-facing `serial` vs `parallel` choice is unaffected). **Frontmatter**: Superscalar.md frontmatter `version: v0.3.0` (added), title bumped from "design draft v0.2" to "design draft v0.3", status line gains "lane-class-aware (v0.3 read/write cap split)" and `§11 Entry 01-05` (was 01-03). **Scope**: minor — Superscalar.md body change + Master/Compact seed cascade. Constellation.md unchanged. Wire unchanged. Per `feedback_release_versioning_cadence.md` — meaningful policy-doc body change with seed cascade is a minor cut, not a patch.

## 변경 이력 (한국어)

- **v2.6.93** (2026-08-08) — 운영자가 물었어요. 로컬 그룹을 골랐는데 왜 대화 대상이 업스트림 쪽 채널로 잡히는가. 같은 질문에 **두 함수가 각자 답하고** 있었어요 — 「이 그룹에 누가 속하나」를요. 탭 렌더러는 숨은 채널을 제외하고 운영자가 저장한 탭 순서를 적용했는데, 전송 대상 해소기는 둘 다 하지 않고 맵 삽입 순서의 첫 멤버를 집었어요. 그래서 **화면 맨 왼쪽 탭과 글이 실제로 닿는 곳이 갈릴 수** 있었고, 숨은 채널이 그룹 대표가 될 수도 있었어요 — 화면에 아예 없는 상대에게 말을 거는 상태예요. 이제 해소기가 **렌더된 그룹을 읽어요.** 대표가 우연이 아니라 구조적으로 «화면의 첫 탭» 이 되고, 고친 뒤 일곱 그룹 전부에서 일치를 실측했어요. 밖으로 나간 건 없어요 — 업스트림 채널들은 앞선 여섯 시간 트래픽이 0이었어요. **잘못된 표시가 잘못된 발신이 되기 전에** 잡힌 거고, 그래서 이건 표시 결함이지 유출이 아니에요. 하나는 **일부러 안 고쳤어요**: 알아보지 못한 역할은 여전히 로컬로 떨어지고, 그 일을 하는 줄에 이제 그렇다고 적혀 있어요. 그 폴백을 없애면 그 채널들이 어느 그룹에도 안 떠서 **화면에서 사라지고**, 부재는 오분류보다 나쁜 고장이에요 — 아무도 볼 수 없는 채널은 아무도 고칠 수 없으니까요. 완화는 대표가 이제 «운영자가 보는 것» 이라는 점이에요. 오분류된 채널은 잘못 분류된 그 자리에 **보이는 채로** 남고, 인터페이스 뒤에서 조용히 선택되지는 않아요.

- **v2.6.92** (2026-08-07) — Constellation v2.4.151 — 로그인 화면이 **오버레이만** 막고 있었어요. 계정 1개가 있고 `loginRequired:true` 인 상태에서 실측했는데, 쿠키 없는 요청에 보드 상태 엔드포인트가 **전체를 그대로** 돌려줬어요 — 예정·완료·검토사안·프로젝트 전부. 개발자 도구도 필요 없었고 `curl` 한 줄이면 됐어요. 화면이 가리고 있던 데이터를 서버는 애초에 안 가리고 있었어요. 보안 통제가 **«보이기 때문에» 있는 것으로 보고되는** 고장 방식이에요. 읽기 두 경로를 운영자 세션으로 막았고 스트리밍 엔드포인트도 같은 게이트에 넣었어요 — 요청 경로만 닫고 스트림을 열어두면 «고쳤다» 고 기록되면서 데이터는 계속 나가요. 웹소켓 옆문은 **파일에 이미 있던 판별자**로 닫았어요. 새 것을 만들지 않았어요: 브라우저는 `Origin` 을 붙이고 라이브러리 클라이언트는 안 붙여요. 이 규격이 교차출처 웹소켓 탈취를 닫을 때 이미 의지했던 구분이라, 브라우저 갈래 업그레이드만 세션을 요구하고 에이전트 연결은 건드리지 않아요. **대조군이 검증의 일부**예요, 사족이 아니에요: `Origin` 없는 업그레이드는 여전히 성립해요. 누출을 닫으면서 에이전트를 전부 끊는 변경도, 누출이 닫혔는지만 보는 시험에서는 초록으로 나오니까요. 가산 계약은 여기서도 유지돼요 — 계정이 0이면 그 층은 존재하지 않으니 요구할 수 없고, 읽기는 통과하되 노출 상태면 한 번 말해요. 로그인 페이지·그 스크립트·신원 엔드포인트는 세션 없이도 닿아요. 인증하는 길까지 가리는 게이트는 그걸 위해 만들어진 사람을 잠가버려요.

- **v2.6.91** (2026-08-07) — 보드 런타임의 자격증명 경계 2건을 고쳤어요. 자동 검토가 찾았고, 이 런타임이 공개 배포판으로 처음 나가기 이틀 전이에요. 운영자 자격증명 파일은 암호 해시를 담는데 **기본 권한으로 쓰고 그 다음에 chmod** 했어요 — 그 사이에 같은 호스트의 다른 사용자가 읽을 수 있는 창이 열려요. 그리고 `mode` 만으로는 안 닫혀요: 그 옵션은 **새로 만들 때만** 적용되니 이미 느슨한 파일을 덮어쓰면 권한이 그대로예요. 이제 임시 파일을 0600 으로 만들어 원자적으로 옮기고, 옮긴 뒤 한 번 더 확인하고, **적재 시에도 경화**해서 이 컷보다 오래된 파일을 신뢰하지 않고 구제해요. 그리고 loopback 을 신원에서 방어층으로 격하했어요. host-local 판정은 프록시 경유를 올바르게 걸러내는데, 걸러낸 뒤에 남는 건 «알려진 운영자» 가 아니라 **«이 호스트의 누군가»** 예요 — 게다가 그 게이트가 지키던 엔드포인트 중 하나가 **bind 주소를 다시 쓰는** 것이라, 로컬 비권한 프로세스가 보드를 전체 인터페이스로 넓힐 수 있었어요. 상태를 바꾸는 관리 엔드포인트 둘은 이제 loopback **과** 운영자 세션을 함께 요구해요. 가산 계약은 그대로예요 — 계정이 0이면 그 층은 존재하지 않으니 요구할 수 없고, 그때는 loopback 으로 통과하되 **노출된 상태라면 매 요청에 그 사실을 말해요.** 조용히 통과하지 않는 게 요점이에요. 세 번째 loopback 사용처는 **의도적으로 안 바꿨고 그 이유를 그 자리에 적었어요** — 당사자가 로컬 워커(운영자가 아니라 에이전트)고, 위험 모형이 원격 정찰이라 loopback 판정으로 닫혀요. 바꾼 둘만 이름 대고 안 바꾼 하나를 안 대면, 의도한 범위가 다음 사람에게 누락으로 읽혀요.

- **v2.6.90** (2026-08-07) — Constellation v2.4.149 · Pantty v0.1.1 — 좌석 구동 참조 런타임이 Constellation 트리를 나와 모듈 루트로 갔어요. 앞 컷이 시작한 승격을 마무리하는 거예요: `constellation/reference/runtime/pantty/` 가 `pantty/` 가 되고, 다른 모듈들의 자기 자산 디렉터리와 나란히 서요. 옮겨도 안전한 이유는 **아무도 그 파일들을 import 하지 않기** 때문이에요 — 전수로 훑어보니 어느 소비자에서도 require·import·spawn 이 없었어요. 자기 워크스페이스 경로를 스스로 계산하는 독립 스크립트고, 저장소 전체에서 기계 결속은 검사기 하나 안의 경로 상수 **한 곳**뿐이었어요. 그러면 위치는 의존이 아니라 순수한 소유 신호고, 소유는 모듈 승격 때 정해졌어요. CHANGELOG 와 README 버전 사슬의 이력 항목은 옛 경로를 **일부러 그대로** 둬요 — 그건 파일이 지금 어디 있는지가 아니라 그 판이 무엇을 말했는지의 기록이라, 고치면 기록을 위조하는 거예요. 가는 길에 가드 둘이 제 몫을 했어요: 재지정 스크립트가 쓰기 전에 앵커를 세서, 이중언어 속성 때문에 경로가 3건 대신 7건 나온 파일에서 멈췄어요. 그리고 docs-meta 축이 히어로 배지는 새 버전인데 페이지 설명은 앞 판을 요약한 채인 걸 잡았어요. 그리고 이동이 옛 배치가 감추고 있던 걸 드러냈어요 — 컴파일된 파이썬 바이트코드가 공개 저장소에 추적되고 있었어요. 기계 특정이고 아무도 읽지 않아서 추적을 해제하고 앞으로 제외해요. 경로를 만지는 순간이 그 안에 얹혀 온 걸 빼내는 자리예요.
